connection: Worker now guarantees required identity through its constructor. This session separates required state from optional state and uses nullable analysis to make that distinction explicit.
objectives: Distinguish required non-nullable state from optional nullable state.
Use an object initializer for optional init-only configuration.
Explain how constructor assignments satisfy non-nullable guarantees.
Handle a nullable value before displaying it.

visuals.title: Nullable means value or no value
visuals.explanation: string? explicitly permits either a string reference or null; callers must account for both states.

visuals.title: Construction guards required state
visuals.explanation: Worker validates identity and name before assigning them, so every successfully created object satisfies those requirements.

visuals.title: Initialization adds optional state
visuals.explanation: The constructor establishes required values first; the object initializer supplies the optional team during the same creation expression.

visuals.title: Null handling narrows uncertainty
visuals.explanation: The null-coalescing operator chooses TeamName when present and a fallback when it is null.

options: The property may intentionally be null
The string is a value type
preQuiz.explanation: Nullable reference annotation makes the optional state part of the contract.

preQuiz.prompt: Why are Id and DisplayName not nullable?
options: They are required and assigned by successful construction
preQuiz.explanation: Constructor validation and assignment establish required non-null state.

preQuiz.prompt: When can an init-only property be assigned?
preQuiz.explanation: init permits assignment during creation while preventing later ordinary assignment.

concept.title: Nullability is a contract
paragraphs: string means callers should expect a string; string? means absence is permitted. Nullable analysis tracks this distinction and warns when code dereferences a maybe-null value without proof.
Annotations do not perform runtime validation, so constructor guards still enforce required inputs.

concept.title: Required and optional initialization differ
paragraphs: Id and DisplayName must exist for every Worker, so they are constructor parameters. TeamName is optional, so it defaults to null and may be supplied by an object initializer.
init keeps the optional choice part of creation rather than allowing unrestricted mutation later.

concept.title: Handle both nullable states
paragraphs: The null-coalescing operator evaluates its left operand and uses the right operand only when the left is null.
That produces a non-null display string without pretending the optional property is always populated.

lab.objective: Add optional team membership without weakening required Worker invariants.
lab.startingCondition: Worker requires Id and DisplayName and has no optional properties.
steps: Predict the default value of a string? property.
Add nullable init-only TeamName to Worker.
Set TeamName to Platform in Program.cs with an object initializer.
Display TeamName with Unassigned as the null fallback.
Test both default-null and initialized states, then build and run.
lab.expectedBehavior: The app displays Team: Platform; a Worker created without a team has null TeamName; 13 tests pass.
lab.validation: dotnet build TimeLedger.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test TimeLedger.sln --configuration Release && dotnet run --project src/TimeLedger.App/TimeLedger.App.csproj --configuration Release --no-build

expectedFiles.why: Initialize and safely display the optional team.

commit: session-06: teach initialization nullability and invariants
review: Required properties remain non-nullable and constructor-initialized.
TeamName is init-only rather than freely mutable.
Tests cover absent and present values.

postQuiz.prompt: What is TeamName immediately after new Worker(id, name) with no initializer?
postQuiz.explanation: Nullable reference properties default to null when not assigned.

postQuiz.prompt: What does ?? do in the display expression?
options: Selects a fallback only when TeamName is null
postQuiz.explanation: It produces a result without mutating the property.

postQuiz.prompt: Why not make DisplayName nullable too?
options: It is required for a valid Worker
postQuiz.explanation: The domain invariant says every Worker has a display name.

reflections: Which Worker values are required versus optional, and why?
What runtime rule is not supplied by nullable annotations alone?
When is a constructor parameter better than an init-only property?
whatBreaks: Removing the nullable annotation misstates the optional contract and creates initialization warnings. Removing constructor assignment for required properties breaks the non-null guarantee. Removing null handling makes future use of TeamName unsafe when no team was supplied.
summary: Nullable annotations describe permitted absence, constructors establish required invariants, object initializers supply optional creation-time state, and null handling turns uncertainty into a safe value.
